QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_4

question.text: Which of the following best describes 'absolute return'?

answer.text: The return of a fund relative to its benchmark index
The rupee amount earned on an investment
The return adjusted for inflation over a specific period
The return after deducting all fees and expenses

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines absolute return as the rupee amount earned on an investment, and then separately defines percentage return as Return on Investment / Original Investment x 100, and annualized return as the conversion of returns to a one-year holding period. So absolute return is specifically the rupee amount, not a percentage or an inflation-adjusted figure. The Trap: Benchmark-relative return and inflation-adjusted (real) return are different concepts; net-of-fees return is also a different idea. Only the rupee amount earned matches the workbook's definition of absolute return. Note: Keep absolute return (rupee amount), percentage return, and annualized return separate when answering — the workbook treats them as three distinct measures.
